attributes.cardDescription: An applicant moving through the hiring pipeline with resume text, skills, interview score, and computed time-to-hire
attributes.readMe:
# Candidate

## Summary
Extends PersonBase with appliedRole, appliedDate, decisionDate, pipeline status (applied | screening | interviewing | offer | hired | rejected), resumeText, skills, overallScore (ScoreField), and offer fields. `timeToHire` is a computed DurationField between appliedDate and decisionDate.

## Import
```ts
import { Candidate } from './candidate';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As a pipeline board card.** `status` (applied | screening | interviewing |
offer | hired | rejected) drives which kanban column the person sits in, and
`boardOrder` persists their position within it.

**2. As the target of the AI commands.** `ExtractResumeCommand` parses
`resumeText` into name/email/phone/appliedRole/skills;
`GenerateInterviewQuestionsCommand` writes a round-specific markdown question
set into `candidate.position.interviewPlan` (see interview-plan.gts) — not
onto the Candidate itself, since the plan belongs to the Position and is
shared across every candidate in that pipeline. Both commands read the resume
**text**, never the PDF.

**3. As the subject of an Offer.** `candidate.offer` ↔ `Offer.candidate` is the
only genuinely bidirectional pair in this app; `offerState` mirrors the offer's
lifecycle as a scalar so the board can read it without resolving the link.

**4. As the interview subject.** `Meeting.candidate` points here, and the board
rolls up every linked Meeting's `interviewScore` into an average.

**5. As the source of a new Employee.** `ApproveOfferCommand` copies name,
email, phone and appliedRole across, then sets `hiredAs`.

## Template Usage
Isolated view shows the pipeline stage, skills pills, a round-type toggle plus
the linked Position's interview plan (read-only, via `<@fields.position.interviewPlan />`), and the raw resume.

**Non-goals:** multi-position applications; EEO/compliance capture; interview scheduling (Meeting owns it); interview question *content* (InterviewPlan, linked from the candidate's Position, owns that — see interview-plan.gts). `boardOrder` is board-presentation state whose home (block vs app) is an open question for the author.
